I got this twin size foldable tatami mattress about 6 months ago. This and a twin size foldable rush grass tatami mat were the initial items I purchased to go on an elevated queen size metal platform bed frame after I got rid of my queen size memory foam mattress, box springs, and bed frame. I was trying to find a way to sleep cooler at night. I had been sleeping poorly in part because I kept waking up overheated and sweaty. My sleep experiment lasted several months. I added 3" of queen size coconut coir mats to provide firmness and breathability. I also added a 1" hemp mattress pad. Since this is a foam mattress it does warm up from body heat, but not nearly as much as an actual memory foam mattress. I no longer wake up at night hot and sweaty. That said, I am considering a more expensive wool or wool/cotton tatami mattress for comfort and temperature regulation.

Installed it on my RAV 4. Easy installation on the roof crossbars (also from Vevor). I think the price point on this item is fairly high, even if it was “on sale”. It is a lightweight fiberglass material, which seems a bit flimsy, but looks like it should hold up for my purposes… hoping so anyway. On the plus side, I’ve already driven well over 160 kms. with it ontop of my car (city & highway) & have not even noticed a difference in sound (noise) or vehicle performance, with it installed. That is a huge plus,, as I will be making a cross country trek with it this summer, & was not going to appreciate extra wind/noise levels along the way. Another plus is the fact that it opens from either side (with a stable foldable rod holding the lid open) giving the advantage of placing it either in the middle of the vehicle roof, or on either the driver or passenger side. It’s also quite easy to move from one side to the other, if you don’t like the initial placement. I bought the smaller model (8 cu. feet) to fit on top of my small SUV, but the interior storage space looks adequate for my extra storage needs.

The Vevor car roof box offers decent value for its price, but the components have a cheap appearance and feel less durable than more expensive brands. The product is not rugged, so it requires careful use, and noticeable scratches upon arrival suggest possible previous returns, even though packaging was protective. Despite these issues, the roof box was functional and reliable for a journey, making it a reasonable choice for those on a budget, as long as expectations for durability remain modest and it is handled with care.
